name: Aminata Diallo
headline: 19-year-old apprentice bricklayer and part-time student, Bamako, Mali
title: A Cousin’s Request for Help
situation: On a Sunday afternoon, Aminata’s cousin Fatoumata visits her rented room. Fatoumata is organizing a naming ceremony for her newborn next week and asks Aminata to help prepare traditional dishes the day before the event. She knows Aminata works long hours but insists it is a family duty. Aminata had planned to use that Sunday to study for her accounting exam, which is in two weeks. The ceremony is important in their culture, and refusing might be seen as disrespectful. Aminata must decide whether to help her cousin or stick to her study plan.

context.relationship_profiles: Fatoumata is Aminata's older maternal cousin, a few years senior, who married young and lives in a nearby compound. She has occasionally checked on Aminata after her mother died, bringing food, but also asks her for help with family events because she knows Aminata is reliable. Aminata feels a quiet obligation to Fatoumata, who is one of the few relatives who acknowledges her work as a builder without condescension.
context.tendencies: When coworkers invite her to evening gatherings, she consistently declines to study, and she has never taken a day off from the construction site except when ill. She once agreed to help her aunt prepare for a wedding, then spent the night catching up on lost study time, a pattern she found exhausting. She avoids spoken commitments that could conflict with her savings schedule.
context.current_state: Aminata worked a ten-hour shift Saturday hauling bricks and arrived home aching, with only four hours of sleep after studying until midnight. She has a practice accounting exam scheduled for Monday evening and still needs to master depreciation calculations, which she finds difficult. Her fund for her sister's relocation is exactly on track, and she fears any disruption.
context.immediate_memories: The baby wrapped in Fatoumata's arms triggers a memory of Aminata at twelve, holding her own infant sister outside the hospital while her mother was dying inside—a day she was pulled from school and never fully returned. Fatoumata's tone as she says 'family duty' evokes a recollection of her father selling his trowel set to pay for that funeral, a tool she now uses every day.
context.reflective_memories: She recalls her mother often saying 'We must show up for family, or we lose them,' but also remembers how her mother's constant attendance at community ceremonies left her stall unattended and accounts neglected, leading to the miscalculated loan. Aminata has internalized that counting and preparation protect against the same faith in goodwill that ruined her family.
